model: recorded (authored by Claude from reading the code; not an API run)
objective_statement: Take one week of a battery's dispatch data (historical operation versus a perfect-foresight benchmark), quantify the revenue gap, attribute it to a primary and a secondary driver, and return two evidence-grounded recommendations as a UI view and a PDF report. Three LLM sub-agents do this, with pandas tools doing the numeric work.
summary: The purpose is clear and the README states it well. Two documented behaviours do not work as described: the custom analysis question never reaches any agent, and the 'model never sees CSV rows' claim is false (see Governance). One analytic scope question is open: half of the loaded scenario/schedule combinations are never analysed.

findings.title: The custom analysis question is accepted but never used
findings.claim: `user_query` is only logged and copied into the report metadata. `data_prep.run`, `analysis.run` and `recommendations.run` take no query parameter, so the UI text box (README line 36) and the `--query` flag (README line 50) change nothing. Example: a user asks why Tuesday evening lost money and receives the same generic report.
findings.why_it_matters: A prominent control that silently does nothing makes the user believe the analysis was steered by their question.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the field and the flag, or pass `user_query` into the Analysis and Recommendation initial messages and have the report state how the question was addressed.

evidence.quote: user_query: str = "Analyze the battery performance data and provide recommendations.",

findings.title: Expected-schedule rows are loaded and cleaned but never analysed
findings.claim: All four scenario/schedule combinations are validated and cleaned, but every analysis tool reads only `historical/cleared` and `perfect/cleared`. The `expected` rows appear only as per-combination revenue totals. If `expected` is the operator's forecast or bid, the gap between expected and cleared is a candidate driver that the primary/secondary attribution cannot see. This depends on what `expected` means in the data, which the repo does not say.
findings.why_it_matters: If forecast or bid error matters, the attribution may blame dispatch timing for something that happened upstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with the data owner what `expected` represents. If it is informative, add an expected-versus-cleared comparison as another input to the gap-driver step; if not, drop those rows early.
